cards.name: SegmentRange
cards.summary: A list of curve segments from one curve that you treat as a unit: read their combined Length and common Type, turn them all into straight lines or Bezier curves with SetType, split each one with a midpoint node (AddNode), or select the nodes that control them for the Shape tool.
use_for: turning a straight-edged polyline trace into curves before smoothing it into an organic logo outline
doubling the node count of a path before a hand-drawn wobble or distortion script
measuring the cut length of selected edges for a vinyl, laser or embroidery quote
selecting a set of segments' nodes so the user can keep editing them with the Shape tool
avoid: moving or editing individual nodes: use the Nodes collection / NodeRange (NodeRange gives back a SegmentRange when you need both)
combining segments from different curves: the range has a single Parent curve
cards.how: Members live on IVGSegmentRange. Get one from a curve's segment collection (ActiveShape.Curve.Segments.All, .Range(Array(1, 3)), .AllExcluding(...)), from NodeRange.SegmentRange, or make an empty one with Application.CreateSegmentRange and fill it with Add / AddRange. Iterate with Count / Item (base 1) or For Each, then apply a bulk change (SetType, AddNode) or selection call.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of segments in the range

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets For Each walk the range

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrSegmentType common to all segments (cdrLineSegment / cdrCurveSegment), presumably cdrMixedSegments (2) when they differ

key_members.name: Length
key_members.use: total length of the segments, in document units

key_members.name: SetType
key_members.use: make every segment a line or a curve in one call

key_members.name: AddNode
key_members.use: insert a node in the middle of each segment

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: append a Segment to the range

key_members.name: AddRange
key_members.use: append all segments of another SegmentRange

key_members.name: Remove
key_members.use: drop the segment at an index from the range

key_members.name: RemoveRange
key_members.use: drop the segments of another range

key_members.name: NodeRange
key_members.use: the NodeRange for the nodes behind these segments

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Curve the segments belong to

key_members.name: CreateSelection
key_members.use: select the controlling nodes (replacing the node selection)

key_members.name: AddToSelection
key_members.use: add the controlling nodes to the node selection

gotchas: Item is base 1 (the typelib says so); Item(0) fails.
Remove / RemoveAll only edit the list; nothing is deleted from the curve. To delete geometry work on the nodes or the SubPath.

AddNode and SetType change the curve, so segment indexes and Segments.Count shift afterwards; rebuild the range from Curve.Segments before a second pass (unverified whether the old range stays valid).
Parent is a Curve, not a Shape: segments from another curve cannot join this range (unverified whether Add raises an error or silently ignores them).
Length is in ActiveDocument.Unit; set the document unit first if you need millimetres.
cards.example:
Dim sr As SegmentRange
Set sr = ActiveShape.Curve.Segments.All
Debug.Print sr.Count & " segments, length " & sr.Length
If sr.Type <> cdrCurveSegment Then sr.SetType cdrCurveSegment
sr.AddNode
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: Segments
cards.summary: The collection of all segments of a curve (Curve.Segments) or of one subpath (SubPath.Segments): count them, walk them one by one, or cut out a SegmentRange of chosen, all, or all-but-some segments for a bulk edit.
use_for: counting straight vs curved edges of a traced logo to decide whether it needs smoothing
walking every edge of a path to measure or label it (dieline, cut path)
building a SegmentRange of all segments to convert them to curves in one go
avoid: node-level edits (move, cusp/smooth): use Curve.Nodes
bulk changes: take a SegmentRange with All / Range rather than looping Item calls
cards.how: Members live on IVGSegments. Reach it from a curve shape: ActiveShape.Curve.Segments (every segment of every subpath) or ActiveShape.Curve.SubPaths(1).Segments (one subpath). Read Count / Item (base 1) / First / Last, loop with For Each, or call All / Range(Array(...)) / AllExcluding(Array(...)) to get a SegmentRange.

key_members.name: Range
key_members.use: SegmentRange from an array of indexes

key_members.name: AllExcluding
key_members.use: SegmentRange of every segment except the listed indexes

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Curve the collection belongs to

gotchas: Only curve shapes have it: ActiveShape.Curve is Nothing / fails for a rectangle, ellipse or text until ConvertToCurves (unverified which of the two).
Item is base 1.
The collection is live: adding nodes or breaking segments while looping changes Count, so collect a SegmentRange first or loop backwards (unverified for For Each).
Parent is typed as Curve even when the collection came from a SubPath (the typelib text says 'parent subpath').
cards.example:
Dim seg As Segment, nLines As Long
For Each seg In ActiveShape.Curve.Segments
    If seg.Type = cdrLineSegment Then nLines = nLines + 1
Next seg
Debug.Print nLines & " of " & ActiveShape.Curve.Segments.Count & " are straight"
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: SelectionInfo
cards.summary: A read-only report on the document's current selection: how many objects and which (FirstShape, SecondShape), what they are (group, text, bitmap, blend / contour / drop shadow / extrude parts, guideline, connector) and what can be done to them (CanApplyFill, CanCreateBlend, CanApplyContour, CanUngroup ...). It is the information CorelDRAW uses to enable menu commands.
use_for: guarding a macro so it only runs when the selection makes sense (two shapes for a blend, text for a type fix)
finding the control object behind a drop shadow, contour or blend group the user clicked
enabling or greying out buttons in a custom docker based on the selection
skipping a batch step when the selection holds locked objects (CanUnlockShapes) or the document cannot print (CanPrint)
avoid: working on objects you collected yourself: test the ShapeRange / Shape directly (Type, CanHaveFill, IsSimpleShape)
changing anything: every member is read-only; act through the Shape / ShapeRange
cards.how: Members live on IVGSelectionInformation. ActiveDocument.SelectionInfo returns it for the document's live selection. Is* members without 'Selected' / 'Present' test the first selected shape; *Selected / *Present test whether any selected shape matches; Can* tell whether a command would work; the shape-valued members (BlendTopShape, ContourGroup, DropShadowControlShape ...) hand back the parts of a selected effect.

key_members.name: IsGroup
key_members.use: the selected shape is a group

key_members.name: IsGroupSelected
key_members.use: any selected shape is a group

key_members.name: IsEditingText
key_members.use: the user is inside a text edit

key_members.name: IsBitmapSelected
key_members.use: a selected shape is a bitmap

key_members.name: CanCreateBlend
key_members.use: the selected shapes can form a blend

key_members.name: CanUngroup
key_members.use: something in the selection can be ungrouped

key_members.name: IsDropShadowGroup
key_members.use: the selected shape is a drop shadow group

key_members.name: DropShadowControlShape
key_members.use: the object casting the selected drop shadow

key_members.name: BlendTopShape
key_members.use: top control shape of the selected blend

gotchas: It always describes the current document selection, not a range a script built: call ShapeRange.CreateSelection first if you want to query your own objects.

Several typelib descriptions are shifted by one line (IsConnector reads 'fitted text', IsFittedTextControl reads 'natural media control', IsNaturalMediaGroup reads 'envelope', CanCloneDropShadow reads 'blend'): trust the member name, not the description (unverified that the names are the correct ones).
Shape-valued members return Nothing when the selection has no such part (unverified; test with Is Nothing before use).

Is* (first selected shape) and Is*Selected / Is*Present (any selected shape) give different answers for mixed selections (unverified that the plain Is* members read the first shape; the typelib says only 'the selected shape').
cards.example:
Dim si As SelectionInfo
Set si = ActiveDocument.SelectionInfo
If si.Count = 2 And si.CanCreateBlend Then
    si.FirstShape.CreateBlend si.SecondShape, 12
ElseIf si.IsDropShadowGroup Then
    Debug.Print "shadow of: " & si.DropShadowControlShape.Name
End If
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: use_for 'skipping locked or unprintable cases' implied per-object printability; CanPrint is document-level, so it now names CanUnlockShapes / CanPrint; the first-shape reading of plain Is* members is marked unverified

cards.name: SeparationPlate
cards.summary: One ink plate of a separated print job (cyan, magenta, yellow, black or a spot colour): switch the plate on or off, set its halftone screen frequency and angle, and choose whether text and graphics overprint on it.
use_for: printing only the plate that changed when one ink needs new film or a new plate
custom screen angles / frequencies per ink to avoid moire on a spot-colour job
overprinting black text or a varnish / white underbase plate
avoid: identifying a plate by Type: the typelib says Type is reserved; use Color
colour-managed proofing on screen: that is a view / proof setting, not separations
cards.how: Members live on IPrnVBASeparationPlate (flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb and also in the CdrPrn library), so object browsers show this visible SeparationPlate class instead. Reach it from the document's print settings: ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations.Plates(i) / .Plates.Item(i).

key_members.name: Color
key_members.use: read-only ink name of the plate

key_members.name: Angle
key_members.use: screen angle in degrees for the plate

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: PrnPlateType, read-only and documented as reserved

gotchas: Plates only matter when PrintSettings.Separations.Enabled is True; set it first.
Per-plate Frequency / Angle are likely ignored unless the advanced screening settings (Separations.AdvancedSettings) are on (unverified).
The plate list is built from the inks the document uses; a spot colour that is not used anywhere has no plate (unverified).
Color is the display name of the ink (a Pantone name for spot plates); compare it exactly (unverified case sensitivity).
cards.example:
Dim i As Long
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations
    .Enabled = True
    For i = 1 To .Plates.Count
        If .Plates.Item(i).Color = "Black" Then .Plates.Item(i).OverprintText = True
        Debug.Print .Plates.Item(i).Color, .Plates.Item(i).Angle
    Next i
End With
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: SeparationPlates
cards.summary: The list of colour separation plates the document's print job will produce, one SeparationPlate per ink; it only offers Count and Item.
use_for: looping over every ink plate to report or switch plates before printing separations
checking how many inks (process + spot) a job will need before sending it to press
avoid: finding which spot colours a design uses: read the document's colours / palette instead, the plate list depends on print settings
For Each loops: no enumerator is harvested, use For i = 1 To Count
cards.how: Members live on IPrnVBASeparationPlates (hidden interface, also in CdrPrn). Reach it as ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations.Plates; take one plate with Item(i).

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of separation plates available for the document

gotchas: No _NewEnum member is harvested, so For Each over Plates may fail; use an index loop.
Item index base is not stated; treat it as base 1 like the rest of the object model (unverified).
Count reflects the current print settings (separations on, colours converted to process or not), so read it after changing those settings (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim seps As Object, i As Long
Set seps = ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Separations
seps.Enabled = True
For i = 1 To seps.Plates.Count
    Debug.Print i, seps.Plates.Item(i).Color, seps.Plates.Item(i).Enabled
Next i
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: Shape
cards.summary: Any object in a CorelDRAW document (rectangle, ellipse, curve, text, bitmap, group, effect group, guideline, symbol instance, or the selection itself): it carries position and size, fill / outline / transparency, stacking and layer, shaping (weld, trim, intersect), live effects (drop shadow, contour, blend, envelope, extrude, lens) and conversions (to curves, to bitmap).
use_for: placing a logo, badge or price tag at exact page coordinates in a layout template
restyling an object's fill and outline and naming it so later scripts can find it
boolean shaping of icons and logo marks (weld, trim, intersect, fillet corners)
adding a drop shadow, inner shadow or contour to a headline or product card
converting text to curves or rasterising an object before a print-ready export
PowerClipping a photo inside a frame shape for a poster or social post
avoid: looping over many objects one by one when a ShapeRange call (ApplyUniformFill, AlignAndDistribute, Group) does it in one step
Shape.Group / Shape.Combine on one object: they act on the selection; build a ShapeRange and call its Group / Combine
ConvertToCurves on text that still needs editing: it is one-way, keep a hidden duplicate
cards.how: Members live on IVGShape. A script never creates a Shape with New: it comes back from Layer.CreateRectangle2 / CreateEllipse2 / CreateArtisticText, ActiveShape, Shapes.Item(i) / FindShape, ShapeRange.Item(i), or from methods that return a new shape (Duplicate, Clone, Weld, Trim, ConvertToBitmapEx, Group). Check Type (cdrShapeType) before touching the type-specific sub-objects (Curve, Text, Bitmap, Rectangle, Symbol).

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrShapeType: which kind of object this is

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: object name; set it so FindShape can find it later

key_members.name: LeftX
key_members.use: left edge in document units (with RightX / TopY / BottomY)

key_members.name: SetPositionEx
key_members.use: move a chosen reference point (cdrCenter, cdrTopLeft ...) to x, y

key_members.name: SetSize
key_members.use: stretch to a width and / or height

key_members.name: Fill
key_members.use: the Fill object: uniform, fountain, pattern, texture

key_members.name: Outline
key_members.use: the Outline object: width, colour, style, arrows

key_members.name: Weld
key_members.use: union with a target shape; returns the new shape

key_members.name: Trim
key_members.use: cut this shape out of a target shape

key_members.name: AddToPowerClip
key_members.use: put this shape inside a container shape

key_members.name: CreateDropShadow
key_members.use: live drop shadow (Opacity 50, Feather 15, offset 0, 0 by default)

key_members.name: ConvertToCurves
key_members.use: turn text / primitives into editable curves (one-way)

key_members.name: ConvertToBitmapEx
key_members.use: rasterise to a bitmap shape (Resolution defaults to 72)

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: remove the shape from the document

gotchas: Coordinates are in ActiveDocument.Unit and Y grows upward from the page's lower edge, unlike Photoshop / Illustrator's top-down Y; set the unit at the start of a script.
PositionX / PositionY / SetPosition use the document's ReferencePoint, which a user or another script may have changed; LeftX / TopY / SetPositionEx are unambiguous.
Group and Combine work on the current selection, not on this shape alone (the typelib says 'group of selected objects' and 'must be part of the same selection').
AddToSelection / RemoveFromSelection do nothing on the selection shape itself (ActiveSelection, Type cdrSelectionShape).
Weld, Trim, Intersect, ConvertToBitmapEx and Group return a new Shape; keep that reference, the old one may be dead (unverified for every case).
ConvertToBitmapEx and ConvertToBitmap default to 72 dpi; pass 300 or more for print.

GetPosition, GetSize, GetBoundingBox and GetMatrix return values through ByRef arguments, which late-bound callers (Python win32com) may not receive; read LeftX / SizeWidth / BoundingBox instead (unverified per binding).

Shape.Duplicate does not copy a live drop shadow (the duplicate reads Effects.Count 0). CreateDropShadow adds a separate group shape (type 16) that holds the shape and its shadow, so Shape.ConvertToBitmapEx on the shape alone leaves the shadow out: convert the type 16 group. Shape.FlattenEffects on a shadowed star gave a dull indigo shape with no shadow (plan runs 2026-10-15 (print_prep.flatten_transparency)).

Two shadow-type effects on one object replace each other: an inner shadow followed by a drop shadow kept only the drop shadow, so put the second on a duplicate (plan runs 2026-10-15 (text_effects.letterpress)). A drop shadow on a live Contour group follows the inner base shape, not the contour: break the group apart first (plan runs 2026-10-15 (cutout_social.sticker_cutout)).

Break Apart on an extrusion group leaves a type-7 group of the wall faces: Shape.UngroupAll() splits it (Shape.Ungroup() returned None there), then Shape.Weld(target, False, False) over the faces one after another gives one complete shape, where the Weld menu item kept only part of them (plan runs 2026-10-15 (text_effects.long_shadow)).
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(0, 0, 4, 2)
s.Name = "badge"
s.Fill.ApplyUniformFill CreateRGBColor(255, 200, 0)
s.SetPositionEx cdrCenter, ActivePage.CenterX, ActivePage.CenterY
s.CreateDropShadow Opacity:=40, Feather:=12, OffsetX:=0.05, OffsetY:=-0.05
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: ShapeRange
cards.summary: A script-held list of shapes that you edit in one call: fill, outline, align and distribute, group, combine, duplicate, step-and-repeat, sort, convert or delete every member together. It is what the selection, FindShapes and Shapes.All give back, and it only holds references, so building or trimming the list never changes the drawing.
use_for: recolouring every object of one type or name on a page in one call (rebrand a template)
aligning and distributing cards, icons or price tags across a layout
grouping the parts of a logo lock-up or combining letters into one curve
step-and-repeat for labels, tickets or tiling patterns
exporting only a chosen set of objects (select the range, export with cdrSelection)
avoid: a single object: use the Shape directly
a permanent named set of objects: group them or put them on their own layer; a ShapeRange lives only while the script runs
cards.how: Members live on IVGShapeRange. Get one from ActiveSelectionRange / ActiveDocument.SelectionRange, Shapes.All / Range / FindShapes, Page.FindShapes, Document.CreateShapeRangeFromArray, or start empty with Application.CreateShapeRange and Add / AddRange shapes. Item takes a 1-based index or a shape name.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of shapes in the range

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: one Shape by 1-based index or by name

key_members.name: Remove
key_members.use: drop the shape at an index from the list (it stays in the document)

key_members.name: Exists
key_members.use: True if a shape is already in the range

key_members.name: FindAnyOfType
key_members.use: sub-range of the shapes of given cdrShapeType values

key_members.name: Sort
key_members.use: reorder the list by a CQL comparison expression

key_members.name: ApplyUniformFill
key_members.use: one flat colour on every shape

key_members.name: SetOutlineProperties
key_members.use: width, colour, caps, joins ... on every shape; untouched arguments keep their values

key_members.name: AlignAndDistribute
key_members.use: align / distribute the shapes like the Align and Distribute docker

key_members.name: Group
key_members.use: group all shapes; returns the group Shape

key_members.name: Combine
key_members.use: combine all shapes into one curve

key_members.name: Duplicate
key_members.use: copy every shape, returns the copies as a ShapeRange

key_members.name: CreateSelection
key_members.use: make these shapes the document selection

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: delete every shape in the range from the document

gotchas: Remove / RemoveAll / RemoveRange only edit the list; Delete and DeleteItem delete shapes from the document.
ActiveSelectionRange is a snapshot of the selection at the moment you read it; selecting other objects later does not change it (unverified).
SetOutlineProperties / SetOutlinePropertiesEx use sentinel defaults (Width -1, NibAngle -9999, cdrTriState -2) meaning 'leave as is': pass only what you want to change.
Group and Combine return a new Shape; the range still lists the old members, which are now children of the group (or gone, after Combine) (unverified for Combine).
Sort and FindShapes queries are CQL strings (for example comparing @shape1.left with @shape2.left); the syntax is not in the harvest (unverified).
Parent is the Application, not a page or layer: a range can mix shapes from several layers or pages, and page-relative calls such as AlignToPage use the active page (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim sr As ShapeRange, g As Shape
Set sr = ActivePage.Shapes.FindShapes(Type:=cdrRectangleShape)
If sr.Count > 0 Then
    sr.ApplyUniformFill CreateRGBColor(20, 90, 200)
    sr.SetOutlineProperties Width:=0.01
    Set g = sr.Group
    g.Name = "cards"
End If
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: Shapes
cards.summary: The live collection of shapes on a layer, page, spread, group or PowerClip: look objects up by index or name, search them with FindShape / FindShapes (by name, type or CQL query, optionally inside groups), or take all or part of them as a ShapeRange.
use_for: finding a named placeholder (logo, price, photo frame) in a template to fill it
walking every object on a layer to audit fonts, colours or bitmap resolution
collecting all text or all bitmaps on a page for a batch fix
avoid: deleting while looping forward: the collection shrinks under you; take Shapes.All first or loop backwards
the user's selection: use ActiveSelectionRange
cards.how: Members live on IVGShapes. Every container has one: ActiveLayer.Shapes, ActivePage.Shapes (all layers of the page), Spread.Shapes, a group's Shape.Shapes, PowerClip.Shapes; SelectableShapes variants on Document / Page / Layer / Spread return only the selectable shapes (presumably skipping locked and hidden objects; the typelib says only 'selectable'). Item accepts a 1-based index or a name.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of shapes in the collection

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: one Shape by 1-based index or by name

key_members.name: FindShape
key_members.use: first shape matching Name / Type / StaticID / CQL Query; Recursive enters groups

key_members.name: FindShapes
key_members.use: ShapeRange of every match (Name, Type, Recursive, Query)

key_members.name: Range
key_members.use: ShapeRange from an array of indexes

key_members.name: AllExcluding
key_members.use: ShapeRange of everything except the listed indexes

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the container (layer, page, shape ...) that owns the collection

gotchas: Index order follows the stacking order; Item(1) is believed to be the frontmost object (unverified).
FindShape returns Nothing when nothing matches; test with Is Nothing before using the result (unverified that it does not raise).
FindShape / FindShapes default Recursive:=True, so they also return shapes inside groups; pass False for top-level objects only.
Page.Shapes spans the page's layers but not the master layers' objects on every page (unverified); Layer.Shapes is limited to one layer.
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, logo As Shape
For Each s In ActiveLayer.Shapes
    If s.Type = cdrTextShape Then Debug.Print s.Name
Next s
Set logo = ActivePage.Shapes.FindShape(Name:="logo")
If Not logo Is Nothing Then logo.Selected = True
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: SelectableShapes 'skip locked and hidden objects' was stated as fact; the typelib only says 'selectable', now marked presumed

cards.name: SnapPoint
cards.summary: One snap point on a shape (a user point you placed, an object point such as a node or centre, a bounding-box point, an edge point or the auto point) or a free point in the document: its position, type, connector direction and stable reference id; user points can be moved and deleted.
use_for: anchoring connector lines to fixed points on flowchart or org-chart boxes
adding named attachment points to a reusable symbol (a pin, a socket, a port)
reading the exact position of a bounding-box corner or centre for precise placement
avoid: moving the shape: move the Shape, not its bounding-box or object snap points
plain coordinates you only need once: read LeftX / CenterX on the Shape
cards.how: Members live on IVGSnapPoint. Get it from a shape's SnapPoints collection (User("id"), BBox(cdrTopMiddle), Object(...), Edge(...), Auto, FindClosest, AddUserSnapPoint / AddUserSnapPointEx), from Shape.FindSnapPoint(ReferenceData), or create a free point with Application.CreateSnapPoint / Document.CreateFreeSnapPoint. Layer.CreateConnector takes two snap points as its ends.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrPointType: user, object, bounding box, edge, free, auto

key_members.name: IsMovable
key_members.use: True when the point may be moved

key_members.name: IsDeletable
key_members.use: True when the point may be deleted

key_members.name: Direction
key_members.use: default connector direction (an angle; degrees presumed, the typelib gives no unit)

key_members.name: CanChangeDirection
key_members.use: True when Direction can be changed

key_members.name: ReferenceData
key_members.use: unique id string; find the point again with Shape.FindSnapPoint

key_members.name: Shape
key_members.use: the shape the point belongs to

key_members.name: Selected
key_members.use: selection state for the Shape tool

key_members.name: Node
key_members.use: the node behind an object snap point

gotchas: Only user snap points are meant to be moved or deleted; check IsMovable / IsDeletable before Move / Delete.

cdrPointType values are bit flags (cdrSnapPointUser 1, Object 2, BBox 4, Edge 8, Free 16, Auto 32) and the legacy cdrFreePoint shares value 1 with cdrSnapPointUser: compare Type with the cdrSnapPoint* names.
Keep ReferenceData, not the object, when you need the point later; references to snap points of a shape that was edited may go stale (unverified).
A free snap point has no owning shape; Shape is presumably Nothing for it (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim sp As SnapPoint, u As SnapPoint
Set sp = ActiveShape.SnapPoints.BBox(cdrTopMiddle)
Debug.Print sp.PositionX, sp.PositionY, sp.ReferenceData
Set u = ActiveShape.SnapPoints.AddUserSnapPointEx("out", ActiveShape.RightX, ActiveShape.CenterY, 0, True)
If u.IsMovable Then u.Move 0.1, 0
cards.source: cdr_api_23 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: Direction key member stated 'in degrees'; the typelib gives no unit, now marked presumed

cards.name: SnapPointRange
cards.summary: A list of snap points you change together: move or delete them all, set one connector direction or the auto-snap state on every point, or make them the snap-point selection. It is what SnapPoints.All, .Selection and .Range(...) return and only holds references.
use_for: shifting all user anchor points of a template box together so connectors re-route
giving every anchor of a flowchart shape the same outgoing direction
clearing old user snap points from a reused symbol before adding new ones
selecting a set of snap points for the Shape tool from a script
avoid: moving the shape: use the Shape's own position members
Remove when you mean Delete: Remove only takes the point out of the list
cards.how: Members live on IVGSnapPointRange. Get one from a shape: ActiveShape.SnapPoints.All (every snap point), .Selection (points selected with the Shape tool) or .Range(Array(p1.ReferenceData, p2.ReferenceData)) (points by reference id; whether a user ID string works there too is unverified). Grow it with Add, shrink it with Remove / RemoveByReference, then call a bulk method.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of snap points in the list

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: add a SnapPoint; returns True on success

key_members.name: Remove
key_members.use: drop the point at an index from the list (point is kept)

key_members.name: RemoveByReference

trimming scan margins on import based on each file's pixel size or dpi
avoid: the same crop for every file: set StructImportOptions.Mode = cdrImportCrop and CropLeft / CropTop / CropWidth / CropHeight instead of writing a handler
keeping the whole image editable: import it whole and PowerClip it into a frame

Scripts do not create it: assign an object implementing IImportCropHandler to StructImportOptions.CropHandler, set Mode = cdrImportCrop, and CorelDRAW passes this object to the handler's Crop method during Layer.Import / ImportEx (flow unverified).

key_members.name: CustomData
key_members.use: read-only: value passed through from StructImportOptions.CustomData

gotchas: All members are long integers, so the crop rectangle is most likely in source pixels, measured from the top-left (unverified).
The handler's Crop returns a Boolean; what False does (skip cropping or cancel the import) is not documented (unverified).
Writing a handler needs a COM-visible class implementing IImportCropHandler; a VBA class module with Implements may work (unverified).
cards.example:
' inside a class that Implements IImportCropHandler (unverified pattern)
Private Function IImportCropHandler_Crop(ByVal o As StructImportCropOptions) As Boolean
    Dim side As Long: side = IIf(o.ImageWidth < o.ImageHeight, o.ImageWidth, o.ImageHeight)
    o.Width = side: o.Height = side
    o.Left = (o.ImageWidth - side) \ 2: o.Top = (o.ImageHeight - side) \ 2
    IImportCropHandler_Crop = True
End Function

bringing in a Word / text file without its formatting so the template styles apply
importing a layered file with its layers kept

use_for: downsampling every imported photo to a size that fits the layout frame at 300 dpi
normalising mixed-resolution scans to one dpi on import
avoid: the same target for every file: set StructImportOptions.Mode = cdrImportResample and ResampleWidth / ResampleDpiX ... directly

Scripts do not create it: assign an object implementing IImportResampleHandler to StructImportOptions.ResampleHandler, set Mode = cdrImportResample, and CorelDRAW passes this object to the handler's Resample method during Layer.Import / ImportEx (flow unverified).

key_members.name: CustomData
key_members.use: read-only: value passed through from StructImportOptions.CustomData

gotchas: Width / Height / DpiX / DpiY probably arrive pre-filled with the source values, so the handler can read them before changing them (unverified).
Values are long integers: pixels and dots per inch (unverified for Width / Height).
The Resample handler returns a Boolean; the effect of returning False is not documented (unverified).
cards.example:
' inside a class that Implements IImportResampleHandler (unverified pattern)
Private Function IImportResampleHandler_Resample(ByVal o As StructImportResampleOptions) As Boolean
    If o.DpiX > 300 Then
        o.Width = o.Width * 300 / o.DpiX: o.Height = o.Height * 300 / o.DpiY
        o.DpiX = 300: o.DpiY = 300
    End If
    IImportResampleHandler_Resample = True
End Function

Without Overwrite = True an existing target file may raise an error in an unattended script (unverified).

o.Filter = cdrCDR

cards.name: StructSpaceProperties
cards.summary: Legacy holder for spacing settings of the classic Text object: character and word spacing, line spacing with its type (percent of character height, points, percent of point size) and space before and after paragraphs. use_for: tightening the leading and letter spacing of a headline block in an older macro
setting consistent paragraph spacing on body copy across many text frames

kerning one character pair: edit the TextRange of those characters

key_members.name: LineSpacingType
key_members.use: cdrLineSpacingType: percent of character height, points, percent of point size

Set sp = ActiveShape.Text.SpaceProperties(cdrAllFrames)
sp.LineSpacingType = cdrPercentOfPointSizeLineSpacing
sp.LineSpacing = 110

cards.name: Style
cards.summary: One style or style set of the document's style sheet (the Object Styles docker): a named, inheritable bundle of fill, outline, character, paragraph, frame or transparency properties. Scripts read and change its properties by name, rename or re-parent it, copy it, serialise it to a string, or delete it; objects using it update with it.
use_for: building a brand style sheet (headline, body, accent fill) that every template object follows
changing a brand colour or outline once and having every object using the style update
auditing which properties a style overrides versus inherits from its parent
avoid: one-off formatting of a single object: set Fill / Outline on the Shape
colour swatches shared across objects: use colour styles (StyleSheet.CreateColorStyle)
cards.how: Members live on IVGStyle. Get it from ActiveDocument.StyleSheet (FindStyle, CreateStyle, CreateStyleSet, Styles.Find, AllStyles.Item), from Shape.Style (the style set applied to a shape) or TextRange.ObjectStyle. Apply it to objects with Shape.ApplyStyle(Name). Category-specific views come from Fill / Outline / Character / Paragraph / Frame / Transparency.

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: internal style name (used by ApplyStyle and FindStyle)

key_members.name: DisplayName
key_members.use: name as the docker shows it

key_members.name: CategoryName
key_members.use: category name, for example fill, outline, character, paragraph, frame, transparency (exact strings unverified)

key_members.name: IsStyleSet
key_members.use: True for a style set (bundle of several categories)

key_members.name: IsObjectDefaults
key_members.use: True for the default style set of an object type

key_members.name: GetAllPropertyNames
key_members.use: names of every property of the style's category

key_members.name: GetOverridePropertyNames
key_members.use: names of properties set locally, not inherited

key_members.name: IsPropertyInherited
key_members.use: True when the value comes from the parent

key_members.name: ClearProperty
key_members.use: remove a local override so the parent value applies

gotchas: Property names are strings defined by CorelDRAW, not by the typelib; call GetAllPropertyNames first instead of guessing (example names like 'fill.type' are unverified).
Category view members (Fill, Outline, Character ...) only make sense for a style of that category or a style set containing it; for others they probably return Nothing (unverified).
Editing a style changes every object that uses it and every derived style; use GetCopy or a new style for a variant.
Shape.Style returns the style set applied to that shape; edits to it may affect only that shape's local style or all users (unverified).
Category name strings ('fill', 'outline', 'character', 'paragraph', 'frame', 'transparency') are believed to be the internal names used by CreateStyle (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim st As Style, n As Variant
Set st = ActiveDocument.StyleSheet.FindStyle("Headline")
If Not st Is Nothing Then
    For Each n In st.GetOverridePropertyNames
        Debug.Print n, st.GetPropertyAsString(n)
    Next n
    ActiveShape.ApplyStyle "Headline"
End If

key_members.use: cdrOutlineJustification: inside, centre or outside the path

key_members.name: BehindFill

WidelineWidth and cdrEnhancedOutline are not explained in the typelib; their exact meaning is unverified.
Changing the style updates every object that uses it, including derived styles.
cards.example:
Dim st As Style
Set st = ActiveDocument.StyleSheet.CreateStyle("outline", , "Keyline 0.5pt")   ' category name unverified
With st.Outline
    .Width = 0.5 / 72        ' points to inches (document unit inches)
    .ScaleWithShape = False
    .BehindFill = True
End With
ActiveShape.ApplyStyle "Keyline 0.5pt"

cards.name: StyleParagraph
cards.summary: The paragraph-category view of a style (presumably alignment, indents, spacing and similar paragraph settings; the typelib lists none): this interface only hands back the generic Style object, through which the paragraph properties are read and written by name.
use_for: reaching the paragraph part of a body-text style set to inspect or adjust it
avoid: typed paragraph properties: there are none here, use Style.GetProperty / SetProperty or TextRange members
cards.how: Members live on IVGStyleParagraph. Reach it from a style or style set: Style.Paragraph. Its only member, Style, returns the generic Style object for name-based property access.

key_members.name: Style
key_members.use: the generic Style object for the paragraph style

gotchas: No typed properties; list the names with Style.GetAllPropertyNames (names unverified).
Style.Paragraph on a style without a paragraph part probably returns Nothing (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim st As Style
Set st = ActiveDocument.StyleSheet.FindStyle("Body text")
If Not st.Paragraph Is Nothing Then
    Debug.Print Join(st.Paragraph.Style.GetOverridePropertyNames, ", ")
End If

cards.name: Styles
cards.summary: A list of styles or style sets from the document's style sheet (top-level styles, style sets, object defaults, all styles, derived styles, or the styles just created from a shape): count them, walk them, or find one by name.
use_for: listing every style in a template to document or audit the brand style sheet
finding a style by name before applying or editing it
avoid: finding across nested styles with Styles.Find on a top-level list: use StyleSheet.AllStyles or StyleSheet.FindStyle
cards.how: Members live on IVGStyles. Returned by StyleSheet.Styles / StyleSets / ObjectDefaults / AllStyles / AllStyleSets, Style.DerivedStyles and the StyleSheet.CreateStyleFrom... / CreateStyleSetFrom... methods.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of styles in the list

gotchas: Item takes a numeric index only (Long); use Find for names.
StyleSheet.Styles and .StyleSets hold top-level entries only; derived styles appear in AllStyles / AllStyleSets or under each parent's DerivedStyles.
Find probably returns Nothing for an unknown name (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim st As Style
For Each st In ActiveDocument.StyleSheet.AllStyles
    Debug.Print st.CategoryName, st.DisplayName
Next st
Debug.Print ActiveDocument.StyleSheet.AllStyleSets.Count & " style sets"

cards.name: StyleSheet
cards.summary: A document's style sheet: all its styles, style sets, object default style sets and colour styles. Scripts find styles, create them from scratch or from a shape, shape range or text range, manage colour styles, and import or export the style sheet to a file to share it between documents.
use_for: building a brand kit (text styles, fill / outline styles, colour styles) into a template by script
copying the house style sheet into incoming client files with Import
creating a style set from a designed sample object and applying it across a layout
renaming or cleaning up colour styles before handing over a file
avoid: formatting a single object once: set its Fill / Outline / text properties directly
palettes for picking colours: palettes are separate from colour styles
cards.how: Members live on IVGStyleSheet. Reach it as ActiveDocument.StyleSheet. Lists come back as Styles; single styles as Style; colour styles as Color objects (AllColorStyles is a Colors collection).

key_members.name: ObjectDefaults
key_members.use: default style sets per object type

key_members.name: FindStyle
key_members.use: a style or style set by name

key_members.name: CreateStyle
key_members.use: new style of a category, optionally based on another

key_members.name: CreateStyleFromShape
key_members.use: styles of a category taken from a shape

key_members.name: CreateStyleSetFromShape
key_members.use: style set taken from a shape

key_members.name: CreateStyleFromTextRange
key_members.use: styles taken from a text range

key_members.name: CreateColorStyle
key_members.use: new colour style, optionally in a harmony

key_members.name: Export
key_members.use: write styles / style sets / defaults / colour styles to a file

key_members.name: Import
key_members.use: read them from a file, optionally merging

gotchas: Export and Import flags (Styles, StyleSets, ObjectDefaults, ColorStyles) all default to False: pass True for the parts you want or the call has nothing to do (unverified whether it fails or writes an empty file).
ReplaceExisting defaults to False; a name clash then probably fails or renames the new style (unverified which).
CreateStyleFrom... methods return a Styles list (one per category created), not a single Style.
Category strings for CreateStyle and CreateStyleFromShape ('fill', 'outline', 'character', 'paragraph', 'frame', 'transparency') are not in the typelib (unverified).
The style sheet file extension used by Export / Import is not in the harvest (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim ss As StyleSheet
Set ss = ActiveDocument.StyleSheet
ss.CreateColorStyle "Brand Blue", CreateRGBColor(0, 82, 165)
ss.CreateStyleSetFromShape ActiveShape, "Card", True
ss.Export "C:\styles\brand_kit.cdss", True, True, False, True   ' extension unverified
Debug.Print ss.AllStyles.Count, ss.AllColorStyles.Count

cards.name: StyleTransparency
cards.summary: Transparency settings stored in a transparency style or the transparency part of a style set: the transparency fill (uniform, fountain, pattern ...), merge mode, uniform level, the transparency of white and black areas of a pattern / texture transparency, and whether it applies to fill, outline or both.
use_for: a reusable 'soft overlay' style (multiply at 30 %) for image captions and photo tints
applying the same gradient fade to many banner backgrounds through one style
avoid: one object's transparency: set Shape.Transparency directly
masking a photo to a shape: PowerClip it
cards.how: Members live on IVGStyleTransparency. Reach it from a style: Style.Transparency. Fill returns a StyleFill describing the transparency's own fill (uniform level, fountain ramp, pattern).

key_members.name: Fill
key_members.use: StyleFill of the transparency (type, fountain, pattern)

key_members.name: WhiteTransparency
key_members.use: transparency of white areas in a pattern / texture transparency

key_members.name: BlackTransparency
key_members.use: transparency of black areas in a pattern / texture transparency

key_members.name: AppliesTo
key_members.use: cdrTransparencyAppliedTo: fill, outline, fill and outline

gotchas: The typelib description of UniformTransparency ('winding rule') and of the interface ('StyleFill class') are copy-paste errors; the member name is the reliable guide (unverified that it holds the uniform level).
The value scale of UniformTransparency / WhiteTransparency / BlackTransparency (0-100 or 0-1) is not documented (unverified).
Mode is a merge (blend) mode; Multiply / Screen results depend on what is underneath, so check the look on the real background.
cards.example:
Dim t As StyleTransparency
Set t = ActiveDocument.StyleSheet.FindStyle("Soft overlay").Transparency
t.Mode = cdrMergeMultiply
t.UniformTransparency = 70   ' scale unverified
t.AppliesTo = cdrApplyToFill
ActiveShape.ApplyStyle "Soft overlay"

cards.name: SubPath
cards.summary: One continuous path inside a curve (a curve has several subpaths when it is combined, like the outer and inner contour of the letter O): its nodes and segments, whether it is closed, its length, area, direction and bounds; it can be reversed, extracted as its own curve, extended with line or Bezier segments, and sampled for points, tangents, perpendiculars, curvature and intersections.
use_for: placing objects at even intervals along a path (dots, stitches, text markers)
finding where two outlines cross for a precise trim or a die-line check
fixing path direction (counter-shapes, compound path winding) before export
pulling the inner contour out of a combined logo shape
avoid: moving or styling the whole object: use the Shape
node-by-node editing of the full curve: Curve.Nodes covers every subpath
cards.how: Members live on IVGSubPath. Reach it from a curve shape: ActiveShape.Curve.SubPaths(i) (base 1), SubPaths.First / Last, or Next / Previous from another subpath. Offsets along the path take an OffsetType (cdrAbsoluteSegmentOffset in document units, cdrRelativeSegmentOffset, presumably 0..1, cdrParamSegmentOffset).

key_members.name: IsClockwise
key_members.use: True when the path runs mostly clockwise

key_members.name: Extract
key_members.use: move the subpath out into a new curve shape

key_members.name: AppendLineSegment
key_members.use: add a straight segment to x, y

key_members.name: AppendCurveSegment2
key_members.use: add a Bezier segment with explicit control points

key_members.name: GetPointAt
key_members.use: Point at an offset along the subpath

key_members.name: GetEvenlySpacedPoints
key_members.use: PointRange of points spaced evenly along the path

key_members.name: IsPointInside
key_members.use: True when x, y lies inside the closed path

key_members.name: Move
key_members.use: shift the subpath by DeltaX, DeltaY

gotchas: Default OffsetType is cdrRelativeSegmentOffset (1) with Offset 0.5; relative offsets are presumably fractions of the subpath length, so 0.5 is halfway (unverified); pass cdrAbsoluteSegmentOffset to measure in document units.
Area is only meaningful for closed subpaths; check Closed first (unverified what an open path returns).
Extract changes the original curve and returns the new shape; indexes of the remaining subpaths shift.
Tangent / perpendicular results are angles, presumably in degrees (unverified); use GetTangentVectorAt for a direction vector.
GetBoundingBox returns through ByRef arguments; late-bound callers should read BoundingBox.
cards.example:
Dim sp As SubPath, pt As Point
Set sp = ActiveShape.Curve.SubPaths(1)
If Not sp.Closed Then sp.Closed = True
Debug.Print sp.Length, sp.Area, sp.IsClockwise
Set pt = sp.GetPointAt(0.5)
ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse2 pt.x, pt.y, 0.05

review.changes: how stated cdrRelativeSegmentOffset as 0..1; the gotcha marks that unverified, now consistent

cards.name: SubPaths
cards.summary: The subpaths of one curve: one entry per continuous path, so a simple shape has one and a combined shape (a letter with a counter, a logo of several parts) has several; count them, loop over them or take one by index.
use_for: finding the inner and outer contours of combined letters or logo marks
checking whether a traced shape is one piece or many before cutting / plotting
looping over every part of a combined curve to measure or fix each one
avoid: breaking the parts into separate objects: Shape.BreakApart does it in one call
cards.how: Members live on IVGSubPaths. Reach it from a curve shape as ActiveShape.Curve.SubPaths; take one with Item(i) (base 1), First or Last, or loop with For Each.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of subpaths in the curve

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Curve the subpaths belong to

gotchas: Only curves have subpaths: convert rectangles, ellipses and text to curves first (or read their DisplayCurve for a read-only copy).
The typelib describes Item as returning 'the specified node'; it returns a SubPath.
Extract, BreakApart or combining changes Count; re-read the collection afterwards.
cards.example:
Dim sp As SubPath
Debug.Print ActiveShape.Curve.SubPaths.Count & " parts"
For Each sp In ActiveShape.Curve.SubPaths
    Debug.Print sp.Index, sp.Closed, sp.Length, sp.IsClockwise
Next sp

cards.name: Symbol
cards.summary: The symbol part of a symbol instance (a shape whose Type is cdrSymbolShape): it points to the shared symbol definition that every instance draws, and can turn this instance back into ordinary shapes.
use_for: reusing one logo, icon or badge many times in a layout so a single edit updates every copy
breaking one instance free to customise it while the others stay linked
listing which symbol each instance on a page uses
avoid: one-off copies you will edit individually: Duplicate the shapes instead
data-driven variations (names, prices): use separate objects or text, symbols are identical copies
cards.how: Members live on IVGSymbol. Reach it through a symbol instance's Shape.Symbol (check Shape.Type = cdrSymbolShape). Create instances by converting artwork with Shape.ConvertToSymbol(Name), which returns the instance shape; copies made with Duplicate stay linked to the same definition (unverified).

key_members.name: Definition
key_members.use: the shared SymbolDefinition this instance shows

key_members.name: RevertToShapes
key_members.use: unlink this instance and return its content as a ShapeRange

gotchas: Editing the Definition changes every instance in the document; revert an instance first if only one should change.
Shape.Symbol on a shape that is not a symbol instance returns Nothing or fails (unverified which); test Type first.
RevertToShapes replaces the instance; the old instance reference is no longer valid (unverified).
Symbols defined in an external linked library update from that library, not from this document (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim inst As Shape, cp As Shape, parts As ShapeRange
Set inst = ActiveShape.ConvertToSymbol("Logo mark")
Set cp = inst.Duplicate(2, 0)
Debug.Print cp.Type = cdrSymbolShape, cp.Symbol.Definition.Name
Set parts = cp.Symbol.RevertToShapes
